coverage.found: Kuwait consumer co-ops are supervised by Social Affairs through ministry-appointed financial and administrative controllers who file periodic reports (Alanba/Aljarida, June 2025). In Nov 2025 the ministry announced automated linkage of co-op financial, admin and stores procedures, so the state system covers this. A co-op law is still only a draft (June 2026). Not a quiet SME buyer. No credit unions found.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: The MOH Health Licensing Dept licenses private dispensaries, medical centres and labs. Owner must be a full-time Kuwaiti doctor (e.gov.kw pages). No 2026 rule or insurer-billing duty found in one search. Insurer billing unchecked.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: About 600 private pharmacies, licensed to individual Kuwaiti pharmacists. The MOH 'Raqib' platform (phase 2 live) monitors psychotropic dispensing, so the state tool covers the controlled-drug core duty. Precursor users not reached. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: PAM Ministerial Decision 1/2025 suspends non-compliant companies (no new permits, no licence updates) = known K03. Found 2026 PAM tightening of expat job-title versus qualification matching, listed as a candidate. No security or cleaning-agency-specific rule found. Security licensing is likely MOI (unverified).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The Central Agency for Public Tenders (Law 49/2016) registers and classifies contractors. Only 2020 complaints and undated registration stats found. No 2026 rule and no site-register duty found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: MOCI Decision 173/2026 (real estate brokers' AML rules) and gold rules = known K01/K02. MOCI Decision 25/2026 gives the DNFBP violation matrix; Kuwait was FATF grey-listed in Feb 2026. Lawyers, accountants and auditors are a new buyer group; their supervisor and goAML duty are unconfirmed. Notaries appear to be state (Ministry of Justice) functions (unverified).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotels and hotel apartments are licensed through the Tourism sector of the Ministry of Information (fee KD 0), needing fire, municipality and commercial licences (e.gov.kw). Hotel requirements were amended Oct 2025. The 2026 Finance Ministry ban on subletting state chalets is a different matter. No guest-register or levy rule found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: One Arabic search on PAFN importer registration returned only Saudi and Egyptian results. Kuwait rules unverified; no budget left to retry in English.

coverage.category: 31. Delivery companies and e-delivery platforms (country-specific)
coverage.found: MOCI Decision 109/2026 took effect 1 Sept 2026 (platform fee cap KD 1, commission 10-17%). A court annulled its penalty article 15 in a suit by talabat. Over 250 small delivery firms petitioned on 12 July 2026. Per-driver duties: nutrition-authority medical certificate, residency tied to the company, vehicle sticker, uniform. MOI warned in Oct 2026 of impoundment for up to 2 months. One candidate.

coverage.category: 32. E-transport / ride-hailing app operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: MOI Resolution 893/2026 requires MOCI licence, prior General Traffic approval, electronic trip and driver records, and in-vehicle cameras with 120-day retention. Candidate listed; belongs to group A category 18.

coverage.category: 33. Fire Force licensing of shops, workshops and industrial areas (country-specific)
coverage.found: Every business must hold and renew a fire licence. Repeated closure campaigns: Farwaniya (24 closed, 57 notices, H1 2026), Capital Governorate (90 closed, 208 notices), Shuwaikh/Jleeb (131 closed); the last two are undated. No 2026 rule change found. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 34. Charities and public-benefit societies' fundraising and reporting (country-specific)
coverage.found: Under Ministerial Decision 1/128 of 2016, only licensed channels may collect donations. Bank-deduction beneficiaries must file a monthly report within 7 working days. Foreign donations need ministry approval under Law 24/1962 art. 30. No 2026 change found. Candidate listed; overlaps group A category 17.

coverage.category: 35. Home-based and micro food businesses (country-specific)
coverage.found: Kuwait Municipality and PAFN warn against unlicensed home food activity; an inspection in Mubarak Al-Kabeer produced 26 violation reports (Alraimedia/Alanba 2026). Rent costs push micro-entrepreneurs toward central kitchens. Rules are not detailed. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 36. PAM expat job-title/qualification alignment and company suspension (country-specific)
coverage.found: PAM Decision 1/2025 suspension triggers and 2026 rules matching workers' degrees to job titles (lexis.ae, Gulf News). Related to K03. Candidate listed.

coverage.category: 37. Environment Public Authority (EPA) licences for industrial and chemical firms (country-specific)
coverage.found: The e.gov.kw EPA pages cover industrial procedures, chemical company registration and release requests. These are state portal services; no 2026 rule or small-firm recurring duty found. Nothing new.

candidates.existing: Free PAFN Raqeb importer portal covers submission and review. A consultant source warns that mismatches between invoice, BAYAN and certificates delay clearance. candidates.name: Small food importer shipment-document and record file for PAFN Raqeb clearance (health, halal and origin certificate matching, Art. 64 record-keeping, fish and shrimp licences)
candidates.trigger: PAFN Ministerial Resolution 6/2023: per-shipment document set (Arts. 15, 18, 19), records duty and fines of KD 100-1,000 (Art. 64); health certificate must predate dispatch; phytosanitary certificate must predate production (IPPC notice Oct 2025); separate fish, shrimp and zubaidi import licences listed in the Raqeb clearance guide

Mostly one-off per-shipment friction, with no periodic report, and the state portal covers the filing itself.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Two searches (Arabic and English) found no Kuwaiti apiary-licensing rule or register. Sources are old Kuwait Times and KUNA pieces: about 500 beekeepers and about 10,000 hives (around 2015-2017), hives hosted on farms, houses and schools, about 18,000 hives imported yearly, mostly from Egypt, and the Kuwait Science Club as the hub. The only regulatory trace is a Kuwaiti honey packer approved for export to Saudi Arabia (SFDA list, 2022), which falls under PAFN food-facility rules. Very small market with no confirmed recurring filing duty. Nothing new; nothing to add beyond the weak candidate below.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Two Arabic and English searches returned only Saudi, Iraqi, Syrian, Palestinian and UAE well-licensing rules, with no Kuwait-specific well-licence or driller register found. Kuwait context: desalination supplies nearly all fresh water; farms may draw only brackish water from the Kuwait Group aquifer (about 1,767 wells in 1994, outdated). The likely competent bodies (Ministry of Electricity and Water, PAAAF, EPA) were not confirmed. Law 21/1995 (EPA) and Law 42/2014 as amended by 99/2015 only cover environmental protection in general. No evidence of a recurring filing duty. Unverified and low prior, so no candidate.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water is state-supplied (MEW desalination and network). A search on tanker and water-transfer licensing surfaced only an e.gov.kw MEW 'TransferingWater' service page, which returned 403 on fetch and whose content is unconfirmed. No evidence of private small water systems with an operator duty.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: The regime is PAFN Ministerial Resolution 6/2023 (in force 1 Sep 2023, 64 articles, repeals Res. 19/2017; text at faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/kuw221743E.pdf). Product registration and importer accounts run on the free PAFN Raqeb portal (raqeb.pafn.gov.kw, Civil ID / Mobile ID login). The per-shipment clearance request needs the temporary customs declaration number, invoice data and attachments: health certificate from the country of origin, halal slaughter certificate for meat, special-food registration, and a separate import licence for fish, shrimp and zubaidi (Raqeb Customs Clearance Request guide, betacweb.pafn.gov.kw/Documents/Guides/Clearance_Request_EN.pdf). Art. 18 lists the shipment documents: customs declaration, certificate of origin, delivery permit, trade licence or import permit, health certificate, packing list, halal certificates, label-claim proofs, temperature records. Art. 64 sets fines of KD 100-1,000 for failing to keep the required records, doubling on repeat within 5 years, with a possible 1-month court suspension of activity (3 months or more on repetition). A shipping advisory (Nov 2025) and an IPPC notice (Oct 2025) say the health certificate must be dated before dispatch, and phytosanitary certificates dated before production are seized. The duty is real and recurring per shipment, but PAFN already provides the free portal and customs brokers file for most importers; I could not find any local importer-side software. Timber and forest-risk commodities (EUDR-type rules) are not relevant to Kuwait as an importer. The fish and shrimp import licence issuer was not confirmed; PAAAF is the likely body.

result.competitor: No Kuwait-specific charity-compliance product found. There are generic or regional tools. Qoyod (Saudi accounting software) has a charity offering with restricted/unrestricted fund accounting, grants and 'National Center reports', where the National Center is Saudi Arabia's. Odoo has an os_charity app (donations, sponsorships, beneficiaries). The state side is a risk: the Ministry of Social Affairs already runs a central aid platform linked to Hawyti (the national ID app), and in June 2025 it announced a larger charity-governance platform, a charity classification scheme and an annual report on every charity. The new National Centre for Charitable and Humanitarian Work may require its own portal. Large charities probably have in-house or bank-provided systems (not checked).
result.duty: Decree-Law 87/2026, the Charitable and Humanitarian Work Law (Aljarida, 13 Sep 2026; fetched), is in force. It covers licensing of fundraising campaigns, collection methods, approved bank accounts, spending controls and financial disclosure, a ban on anonymous-source donations, and protection of donor data. Existing societies and mabarrat must regularize within the periods the law sets, and the executive regulations are due within 6 months. The article gives no fine amounts. It mentions judicial-police powers for Centre staff and prosecution of the crimes the law defines. Rules already in place under the earlier ministry regime (from a search snippet, Alrai/Aljarida): daily collections from donation devices must be recorded and deposited; a monthly report of bank-deduction collections by licensed project is due within 7 working days of the next month; only ministry-approved bank accounts may be used; donor name and date must be recorded; donation links may appear only on the charity's official website. The Ramadan 2026 circular bans collecting inside mosques and requires prior approval for any other location. Report formats and frequency under the new law: not yet published.
result.market: Ministry figures quoted in the press, with dates unclear: 60 charitable and humanitarian societies plus 150 mabarrat (Undersecretary Al-Shuaib); another report puts registered charitable societies at 73. Alrai (2026) mentions about 50 societies and mabarrat working in disaster support. That gives roughly 200–230 entities. Public-benefit associations under the separate 1962 law are not counted here.
result.reason: The duty is real. Decree-Law 87/2026 (13 Sep 2026) requires licensed fundraising campaigns, approved bank accounts and financial disclosure, and existing bodies must regularize. Ministry rules already require donor details on every donation and a monthly report on bank-deduction collections within 7 working days. However, the executive regulations, report formats and penalties are not due until about March 2027. The Ministry is building a central charity platform with an annual report on every charity, which could take over the core job. Software for charities already exists (Qoyod, Odoo os_charity), though none of it is Kuwait-specific. The market is very small: about 60–73 registered charitable societies plus about 150 mabarrat (charitable foundations).

result.competitor: Nobody was found offering a Kuwait-specific tool for 'MOCI digital-commerce registration plus compliance file'. However, registration will almost certainly run through a free MOCI or e.gov.kw service. Payment gateways such as MyFatoorah, which the law effectively makes mandatory since providers must be CBK-licensed, already turn every payment link into a downloadable official invoice. That covers most of the invoicing job for Instagram and WhatsApp sellers. Whether those invoices meet any Arabic-content rule is unverified. Arabic searches for a Kuwaiti e-invoice tool for Instagram stores returned only Saudi ZATCA material. No dedicated tool for influencer-agreement record-keeping was found.
result.duty: Decree-Law 10/2026 on digital commerce, published in the Official Gazette (Kuwait Al-Youm) on 1 Mar 2026. Sources confirm these duties: MOCI registration or licence before any digital commerce, including social-media selling; disclosure of name, commercial-register data and contact details in stores and ads; 14-day withdrawal right; payments only through CBK-licensed providers; influencer data, records and agreements kept at least 5 years and shown to MOCI on request. Penalties under Art. 39: prison up to 1 year and/or fine of KD 1,000-10,000, doubled for repeat offences, plus confiscation and closure. Not verified against the gazette text: the Arabic e-invoice duty for every transaction (Art. 12, which so far appears only in blogs, and the Al-Rai summary omits invoices), the article numbers in the claim, and any small-seller exemption. The effective date is disputed: Al-Rai and Zawya say 6 months after publication, about Sep 2026; Tamimi, as summarised in search results, says 1 month after the executive regulations, which were still unpublished as of late Sep 2026. A separate measure, MOCI Ministerial Decision 109/2026 (in force 8 Jul 2026), covers platforms and delivery apps (e-invoices, complaint records, commission caps), not individual sellers.
result.market: Not found. There is no official count of social-commerce or home-business sellers in Kuwait in the sources reached; the e.gov.kw pages carry no such figures. The buyer group is widely described as large but informal, and the number of sellers who will register is unknown until the regulations and portal launch.
result.reason: The law is real. Decree-Law 10/2026 was published 1 Mar 2026 with 45 articles, and it requires MOCI registration or a licence before any digital commerce, social-media selling included. Art. 39 sets prison up to 1 year and/or fines of KD 1,000-10,000. Records of influencer agreements must be kept 5 years. But the operative workflow can't be checked yet. The executive regulations and the registration portal were not found as of late Sep 2026. Sources disagree on the start date: Al-Rai and Zawya say 6 months after publication, the claim says 1 month after the regulations. The Arabic e-invoice duty and its article number appear only in blogs. On competition, the law makes sellers use CBK-licensed payment providers. MyFatoorah-style payment links already produce official invoices, which shrinks the gap to registration paperwork, likely done on a free MOCI portal. Seller counts were not found. Low willingness to pay.

result.competitor: Camera recording and storage is sold by local AI dashcam and fleet telematics vendors, for example Telox Gulf (Kuwait City; GPS, AI dashcams, driver monitoring). Generic MDVR cloud platforms also exist. Trip, driver and passenger logs are kept by the platforms themselves (Uber, which entered Kuwait in September 2026, Careem, Talyaa and others). No dedicated compliance-file tool for small operators was found, but that is a thin gap.
result.duty: MOI Resolution 893/2026 (Kuwait Al-Youm, in force 5 Jul 2026). Companies must have an MOCI licence, General Traffic Department approval and an approved office. They must keep an electronic register of trips, vehicles, drivers, users and times that Traffic can view or copy, fit in-vehicle cameras with at least 120 days of recordings, and hand passenger data to authorities on request. Vehicles: at most 3 years old at entry for citizen drivers, out of service at 7 years. Driver permits: renewed every year, clean record required. Existing firms had 3 months to comply (until about 5 Oct 2026). Penalty: a warning, then the app can be cancelled or blocked if the breach is not fixed within 1 month; driver permits can be withdrawn. No fines and no periodic reporting were stated. Official gazette text not seen; details come from Al-Rai, ARY and HFW.
result.market: No official count found (not_reached; searched in Arabic and English). The only indicators are small: a report of 50+ taxi-company owners protesting at the MOI, and a handful of licensed apps. The likely market is tens to low hundreds of companies.
result.reason: The duty is real. Two press reports and an HFW law-firm brief say MOI Resolution 893/2026 took effect on publication on 5 Jul 2026, replacing 724/2020. It requires: in-vehicle cameras with at least 120 days of recordings; electronic records of trips, vehicles and drivers that Traffic can inspect; vehicles out of service at 7 years; annual driver permits. Existing firms had 3 months to comply, a deadline that passed about 5 Oct 2026. There are no periodic reports. Sanctions are a warning, then app blocking or permit withdrawal. The camera storage is a hardware job that local AI dashcam and fleet vendors already sell (Telox Gulf, Kuwait). Trip logs live in the platforms' own apps. No count of operators was found, only a hint that the pool is small (a report of 50+ taxi-company owners). Software adds little on top, so the score is low.

result.competitor: No Kuwait-specific delivery-compliance product was found. Generic fleet and driver tools with document-expiry alerts exist (Kazifleet, Onde driver document expiry check). Kuwait delivery-management software (Blink, Riders, Vroom) covers dispatch, not compliance. Custom systems with document-expiry alerts are commissioned via Mostaql/Khamsat.
result.duty: MOI traffic licensing conditions for delivery firms: vehicles under 7 years and motorbikes under 4, yellow plates, company stickers, uniforms, health certificates, helmets and reflective gear, no highways for bikes, fleet caps and a freeze on new vehicle licences. Oct 2026 MOI warning: firms must educate and monitor riders, and violating vehicles face 2-month impoundment. No periodic report to authorities was found. MOCI Decision 109/2026 (in force 1 Sept 2026) caps platform fees and commissions and falls on platforms, not on delivery SMEs. The Administrative Court annulled its penalty article 15.
result.market: About 610 delivery companies with about 12,000 cars and motorbikes (Al-Rai, Jan 2023), 70% of them SMEs. 250+ SME delivery firms petitioned MOCI in July 2026 (Al-Jarida). No current register figure was found.
result.reason: The duties exist, but they are licensing conditions plus police enforcement, not a recurring filing. MOI conditions include vehicle-age limits, yellow plates, stickers, uniforms, health certificates and a cap on new licences. On 4-5 Oct 2026 MOI told firms to educate and monitor their riders, with 2-month impoundment for violations. No formal reporting duty was found. MOCI Decision 109/2026 (KD1 fee cap, 10-17% commissions) binds platforms, and the court annulled its penalty article. About 610 firms (2023), 70% SMEs; 250+ SME firms petitioned in 2026. No Kuwait-specific compliance tool was found, but generic fleet tools (Kazifleet, Onde) already track document expiry. Small firms with low margins and freelancers building custom systems mean weak willingness to pay.

Duty is real: Law 106/2013 covers DNFBPs, and MOCI has a violation-matrix decision (Kuwait Times; reported as No. 25 of 2026, though MOCI site says 2025, so year is unclear). Fines KD 200 to 50,000, up to 500,000 for high-danger breaches. Supervision is split: MOCI for accountants, Lawyers Association (SRO) for lawyers, no AML supervisor named for auditors (Baker Tilly). MOCI enforcement so far hit jewelers and real estate brokers, not professional offices. I found no source on goAML registration, a 2-business-day STR rule or office counts. Competition: FOCAL (getfocal.ai) markets Kuwait AML tooling, and KPMG and Baker Tilly sell services. Buyer is fragmented, supervision is thin and willingness to pay is uncertain.

Duty is real: Kuwait Fire Force requires a fire licence for commercial premises. The e.gov.kw service page for renewing a commercial/professional activity fire licence exists (fetch returned 403). Closures after warnings are routine (June 2024: 76 premises closed). Not verified: validity period, fees, penalty schedule, the number of businesses, and any existing reminder tools or PRO/consultant market. Fee and validity could not be confirmed. The licence appears tied to the landlord's licence and often handled by PRO offices. It is a thin, low-frequency, per-premises workflow, and the market looks fragmented with many informal, often expatriate-run small shops. Willingness to pay for a reminder tool is doubtful. Score stays low.

The duty is real. PAM Ministerial Resolution 1/2025 (Art. 47 clause 3) blocks new permits and licence updates for firms with inactive licences, blocked files or no registered address. Circular 1/2025 froze qualification and job-title amendments, and a 2026 guide says amendments are allowed again from 2 June 2026 when qualification, title and work are compatible. These are secondary sources only. I did not find the PAM text. This is event-driven, not a fixed recurring filing. The state Ashal portal shows status. Keka already markets Kuwait permit and residency expiry tracking. The qualification rules look like a per-worker check, so the niche is narrow. I did not search for local PRO software, and no market count was found. Overlap with K03 is high, so this is a feature of K03 more than a new product.

Raqeb is a real PAFN importer portal with company registration, clearance requests, and agent/broker access (raqeb.pafn.gov.kw). The Resolution 6/2023 text (Art. 64 fines, Arts. 15/18/19) could not be read because the FAOLEX PDF returned only binary. The clearance guide PDF was also unreadable, so I could not check fish/shrimp licences or whether Raqeb pre-checks documents. Arabic competitor search found no Kuwaiti importer-side software. No importer or broker count was found. The friction is per-shipment, not a periodic filing. The free state portal handles the filing, brokers already do the work, and willingness to pay is doubtful. Score stays at 3.
